title: Configure VLANs for Sales and Accounts
realWorldScenario: A small company has two departments, Sales and Accounts, connected to the same physical switch. Management requires these departments to be logically separated so that Sales cannot access Accounts' network resources and vice versa, reducing unnecessary broadcast traffic and improving security.
problemStatement: Both departments currently share the same broadcast domain on SW1. Any device can communicate with any other device, and sensitive Accounts data is exposed to Sales PCs. The company needs logical separation using VLANs.
businessImpact: Poor network segmentation exposes sensitive financial data to unauthorized departments and wastes bandwidth on unnecessary broadcast traffic. Compliance requirements may mandate network segmentation.
objectives: Create VLAN 10 for Sales and VLAN 20 for Accounts, assign appropriate access ports to each VLAN, verify VLAN membership, and test inter-VLAN isolation.
learningObjectives: Understand what VLANs are and why they are used
Create and name VLANs on a switch
Verify VLAN configuration using show commands
Understand that VLANs create separate broadcast domains
Recognize that inter-VLAN communication requires a router (Layer 3)
prerequisites: Basic understanding of switches and how they forward frames
Knowledge of what a broadcast domain is
concepts: Broadcast domains and how VLANs segment them
skills: Create VLANs on a Cisco switch

steps.title: Inspect Current Switch State
steps.instruction: On SW1, check the current VLAN database. Run: show vlan brief. Observe that no custom VLANs exist yet - only the default VLAN 1 is present.
steps.why: Before creating VLANs, you need to understand the current state. This is a fundamental network engineering practice: always inspect before making changes.
hints: The default VLAN (VLAN 1) contains all switch ports initially
Notice there are no custom VLANs yet

commonMistakes.mistake: Not checking existing state before making changes
commonMistakes.solution: Always inspect current configuration before modifying it

steps.completionCondition: Student runs show vlan brief and observes no custom VLANs

steps.title: Create VLAN 10 for Sales Department
steps.instruction: Create VLAN 10 and name it SALES. On SW1: enable, configure terminal, vlan 10, name SALES, end, write memory.
steps.why: VLAN 10 will be the logical broadcast domain for the Sales department. Giving it a descriptive name helps network administrators identify its purpose.
steps.expectedOutput: VLAN 10 created and named 'SALES'. Configuration saved.
hints: VLANs are created in global configuration mode
Use 'write memory' to save the configuration so it persists after reload

commonMistakes.solution: Always assign a descriptive name when creating a VLAN

commonMistakes.mistake: Not saving configuration with write memory
commonMistakes.solution: Always save configuration before exiting to prevent loss on reload

steps.completionCondition: VLAN 10 named SALES exists on SW1

steps.title: Create VLAN 20 for Accounts Department
steps.instruction: Create VLAN 20 and name it ACCOUNTS. Follow the same process as VLAN 10. On SW1: configure terminal, vlan 20, name ACCOUNTS, end, write memory.
steps.why: VLAN 20 will isolate the Accounts department's traffic from Sales. Each department gets its own broadcast domain.
steps.expectedOutput: VLAN 20 created and named 'ACCOUNTS'. Configuration saved.
hints: Use the same vlan command pattern for all VLANs
Each VLAN needs a unique ID and descriptive name

commonMistakes.mistake: Creating VLAN 20 with the wrong name
commonMistakes.solution: Double-check the VLAN name matches the department

steps.completionCondition: VLAN 20 named ACCOUNTS exists on SW1

steps.title: Assign Ports to VLANs
steps.instruction: Assign switch ports to VLANs. On SW1: configure terminal, interface FastEthernet0/1, switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 10, interface FastEthernet0/2, switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 20, interface FastEthernet0/3, switchport mode access, switchport access vlan 10, end, write memory.
steps.why: Creating VLANs is not enough - you must assign ports to them. Access ports belong to a single VLAN. Fa0/1 and Fa0/3 go to Sales (VLAN 10), Fa0/2 goes to Accounts (VLAN 20).
steps.expectedOutput: All three switch ports assigned to correct VLANs. Configuration saved.
hints: Each port must be in access mode before assigning a VLAN
Remember the order: switchport mode access, then switchport access vlan
PC-SALES and PC-MGMT are both on VLAN 10 (Fa0/1 and Fa0/3)

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting to set switchport mode access first
commonMistakes.solution: Always set the port mode before assigning the VLAN
Double-check which department each port belongs to

steps.completionCondition: All ports correctly assigned to VLANs

steps.title: Configure IP Addresses on PCs
steps.instruction: Configure IP addresses on all three PCs. PC-SALES: 192.168.10.10/24, PC-ACCOUNTS: 192.168.20.10/24, PC-MGMT: 192.168.10.20/24.
steps.why: Each device needs an IP address in its VLAN's subnet. VLAN 10 devices use 192.168.10.x, VLAN 20 devices use 192.168.20.x.
steps.expectedOutput: All PCs configured with correct IP addresses
hints: PC-SALES and PC-MGMT are both in VLAN 10

commonMistakes.mistake: Assigning PC-ACCOUNTS an IP from VLAN 10 subnet
commonMistakes.solution: Accounts must use 192.168.20.x because it's in VLAN 20

steps.completionCondition: All PCs have correct IP addresses matching their VLAN

steps.title: Verify VLAN Configuration
steps.instruction: On SW1, run 'show vlan brief' to verify all VLANs and port assignments are correct.
steps.why: Verification is critical. The show vlan brief command shows all VLANs, their names, status, and which ports belong to each VLAN.
steps.expectedOutput:
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -------------------
1    default                          active    
10   SALES                            active    Fa0/1, Fa0/3
20   ACCOUNTS                         active    Fa0/2
hints: VLAN 1 should show no ports if they were all reassigned
Verify both VLANs are present and ports are correctly listed

commonMistakes.mistake: Ports not showing under correct VLAN
commonMistakes.solution: Re-check the switchport access vlan commands for each port

steps.completionCondition: VLAN 10 shows Fa0/1 and Fa0/3, VLAN 20 shows Fa0/2

steps.title: Test Intra-VLAN Connectivity
steps.instruction: Test that PCs within the same VLAN can communicate. From PC-SALES, ping PC-MGMT (both on VLAN 10). From PC-MGMT, ping PC-SALES.
steps.why: Devices in the same VLAN are in the same broadcast domain and should be able to communicate directly. This confirms the VLAN configuration is correct.
hints: PC-SALES (192.168.10.10) and PC-MGMT (192.168.10.20) are both in VLAN 10
They should be able to ping each other because they share the same broadcast domain
steps.completionCondition: Ping replies received between PC-SALES and PC-MGMT

steps.title: Test Inter-VLAN Isolation
steps.instruction: Test that PCs in different VLANs CANNOT communicate. From PC-SALES (VLAN 10), ping PC-ACCOUNTS (VLAN 20). Then from PC-ACCOUNTS, ping PC-SALES.
steps.why: This is the whole point of VLANs - logical separation. Without a router (Layer 3 device), PCs in different VLANs cannot communicate because they are on different broadcast domains.
steps.expectedOutput: Request timed out (because PC-ACCOUNTS is on a different VLAN)
hints: PC-SALES is on VLAN 10, PC-ACCOUNTS is on VLAN 20
Different VLANs = different broadcast domains = no direct communication
To enable inter-VLAN communication, you would need a router (Layer 3 switching or router-on-a-stick)

commonMistakes.mistake: Ping succeeds when it should fail
commonMistakes.solution: Verify VLAN assignments on switch ports and IP configurations on PCs

steps.completionCondition: Ping from PC-SALES to PC-ACCOUNTS times out (isolation confirmed)

steps.title: Understand the Result
steps.instruction: Summarize the results: Sales and Accounts are now separated. Within VLAN 10, PC-SALES and PC-MGMT can communicate. Between VLAN 10 and VLAN 20, communication is blocked. No router is needed for this isolation to work.
steps.why: Understanding WHY things work is as important as HOW they work. VLANs create separate broadcast domains at Layer 2, which prevents unicast and broadcast traffic from crossing VLAN boundaries.
steps.expectedOutput: Confirmed: VLANs 10 and 20 exist, ports correctly assigned, inter-VLAN traffic blocked
steps.completionCondition: Student correctly explains VLAN isolation results

commonErrors.error: PCs in different VLANs can ping each other
troubleshootingSteps: 1. Verify switch ports are in the correct VLAN (show vlan brief)
2. Check that switchport mode access is configured on each port
3. Verify switchport access vlan assignment matches the department
4. Confirm PC IP addresses are in the correct VLAN subnets
possibleCauses: Ports not assigned to correct VLAN
Switchport mode not set to access
commonErrors.fix: Re-assign ports to correct VLANs using switchport access vlan command
commonErrors.verificationAfterFix: Run show vlan brief and ping test again

commonErrors.error: PCs in same VLAN cannot ping each other
troubleshootingSteps: 1. Verify both PCs are on the same VLAN (show vlan brief)
2. Check IP addresses are in same subnet
possibleCauses: Port not assigned to correct VLAN
commonErrors.fix: Correct VLAN assignment or IP address

faults.description: Port Fa0/2 is accidentally assigned to VLAN 10 instead of VLAN 20

finalVerification.successCriteria: VLAN 10 (SALES) and VLAN 20 (ACCOUNTS) are created, ports correctly assigned, and inter-VLAN isolation is confirmed.
finalVerification.completionCriteria: Student has created both VLANs, assigned ports, configured PC IPs, verified intra-VLAN connectivity, and confirmed inter-VLAN isolation.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is the primary purpose of a VLAN?
options: To create separate broadcast domains on a single switch
knowledgeCheck.correctAnswer: To create separate broadcast domains on a single switch
knowledgeCheck.explanation: VLANs allow a single physical switch to function as multiple logical switches, each with its own broadcast domain.

knowledgeCheck.question: Can PCs in different VLANs communicate without a router?
options: No, they are on different broadcast domains
Only if they have the same IP
Yes, if the switch is fast enough
knowledgeCheck.correctAnswer: No, they are on different broadcast domains
knowledgeCheck.explanation: VLANs create separate Layer 2 broadcast domains. Without a Layer 3 device (router), PCs in different VLANs cannot communicate because switches do not forward traffic between different broadcast domains.

knowledgeCheck.question: What command would you use to verify VLAN assignments on a switch?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The 'show vlan brief' command displays all VLANs, their names, status, and assigned ports.

knowledgeCheck.question: What switch port mode is required for a PC connection?
knowledgeCheck.explanation: Access ports belong to a single VLAN and are used for end-device connections like PCs, printers, and servers.
